title: Etale inertia slices of finite generically free normal quotients
statement:
Let $Y$ be a regular Noetherian scheme [def-weil-regular-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], let $X$ be a normal Noetherian scheme (all its local rings are integrally closed domains [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]), and let a finite group $G$ act on $X$. Suppose $q:X\to Y$ is a finite surjective quotient with invariant structure sheaf and orbit geometric fibres [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], and the action is generically free (free on a dense invariant open). Fix a geometric point $\bar x$ above $\bar y$ [def-weil-geometric-point] and put $H=\operatorname{Stab}_G(\bar x)$. For every prescribed pointed etale neighbourhood $T_0\to Y$ there are a pointed affine etale refinement $T\to T_0$, an affine normal integral Noetherian scheme $V$ [def-pc-integral-scheme], an $H$-action on $V$, and an $H$-equivariant pointed etale map $v:V\to X$, with a finite surjective morphism $p:V\to T$ satisfying $qv=(T\to Y)p$. The scheme $T$ is integral regular Noetherian, and $p$ has invariant structure sheaf and orbit geometric fibres for $H$. The action of $H$ on $V$ is faithful. For every dense open $U\subseteq Y$ over which $q$ is etale, the map $V\times_YU\to T\times_YU$ is a connected finite etale $H$-torsor (the action is simply transitive on every geometric fibre) [def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois, def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-etale-morphism]. If $|H|$ is invertible in $\kappa(x)$, $T$ can be chosen so that $|H|$ is invertible on $T$.

Put $R=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{Y,\bar y}$ and $C=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{X,\bar x}$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. The pointed maps identify these with the strict local rings of $T$ and $V$, respectively. The ring $C$ is a finite normal local $R$-algebra, its induced $H$-action is faithful, and the canonical map identifies $R=C^H$. Here $C^H=\{c:h(c)=c\text{ for every }h\in H\}$. No normal crossings boundary, regularity of $X$, excellence, or invertibility of $|G|$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0BST (lemma-inertia-invariants-etale), proof: etale-local product decomposition permuted by G and identification of the selected component invariants with the base. Normal generically free finite-scheme specialization, with further pointed etale refinement and strict localization; compare ILO VI paragraph following 3.5, printed p.74.

proof.text: Choose an affine open $Y_a=\operatorname{Spec}A$ containing $y$, and an affine open $T_a=\operatorname{Spec}A_0$ of the prescribed $T_0\times_Y Y_a$ containing its pointing. Open immersions and compositions are etale [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. Write $X_a=q^{-1}Y_a=\operatorname{Spec}D$; finiteness and this affineness follow from [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence]. The quotient hypothesis gives $A=D^G$. The ring $A$ is Noetherian by [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth]. The etale algebra $A_0$ is finitely presented by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-finite-presentation-localization], hence Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. Set $D_0=A_0\otimes_A D$, a finite $A_0$-module (tensor the given finite generating family). Etale flatness and flat base change of invariants give $A_0=D_0^G$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-flat, lem-dl-a1-flat-base-change-finite-invariants]. All points and maps retain the original algebraically closed field $\Omega$.

source.place: Tag 0BST (lemma-inertia-invariants-etale), first etale-base-change reduction; affine preparation and the prescribed neighbourhood

proof.text: Apply [lem-dl-a1-geometric-point-etale-idempotents] to the finite algebra $D_0/A_0$ and the given point $A_0\to\Omega$. It gives a pointed etale algebra $B$ and orthogonal idempotents in $S=B\otimes_{A_0}D_0$, one for each lift $t:D_0\to\Omega$, separating exactly those lifts. There is at least one lift, the prescribed $\bar x$. The composite $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale, so $B$ is Noetherian by finite presentation and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. Apply [lem-sbc-etale-regular-divisor-base-change] with auxiliary element $g=1$: $A$ is regular, multiplication by $1$ is injective and $A/(1)=0$ is regular (its spectrum is empty). Thus $B$ is regular. By [rem-pc-regular-normal], its finitely many irreducible components are open and closed and normal integral. Replace $\operatorname{Spec}B$ by the component containing the pointing. This remains affine, regular and Noetherian, and its ring $B$ is a domain. Restrict the idempotents and $S$ accordingly. Flat base change again gives $S^G=B$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-flat, lem-dl-a1-flat-base-change-finite-invariants].

source.place: Tags 00UJ/00UL, pointed finite-algebra splitting; Tag 07NF regularity under etale maps; properties.tex Tag 033M, normal components

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak p=\ker(B\to\Omega)$. Each idempotent factor has exactly one $\Omega$-valued point above the given point of $B$, by its separating evaluation formula. The map $B\to S$ is finite, hence integral [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral]; this also holds for each quotient factor. Every prime of a factor above $\mathfrak p$ admits such an $\Omega$-valued lift by [lem-dl-a1-integral-geometric-point-existence], so each factor has exactly one prime over $\mathfrak p$. Its residue extension is purely inseparable by [lem-dl-a1-unique-geometric-point-pure-residue]. Apply [lem-dl-a1-equivariant-fibre-product-refinement] to this product decomposition. After a principal localization $B\to B_b$, $b\notin\mathfrak p$, there is a product $S=\prod_j S_j$ permuted by $G$, each factor having exactly one prime over $\mathfrak p$, with purely inseparable residue extension. Relabel the chosen point into $S_1$. In this paragraph replace $B,S$ by their indicated localizations. The base stays an affine regular Noetherian domain. Flat base change of invariants still gives $S^G=B$.

source.place: Tag 0BST (lemma-inertia-invariants-etale), geometric-point splitting and equivariant refinement paragraphs; Tag 0BRH flat invariants

proof.text: Apply [lem-dl-a1-transitive-product-inertia-component] to this product, $B=S^G$ and $\mathfrak p$. It says that the inertia subgroup $I$ at the selected prime is the stabilizer of $S_1$, that the factors form a transitive $G$-set, and that projection identifies $B\simeq S_1^I$. Here $I=H$: a geometric point is a prime together with an embedding of its residue field into $\Omega$, so fixing that geometric point means stabilizing the prime and inducing the identity on its residue field. A lift to $X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}B$ is fixed by $g$ exactly when its projection to $X$ is fixed, because $g$ is the identity on $B$. Define $T=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $V=\operatorname{Spec}S_1$ and $p:V\to T$. The factor is an open and closed subscheme of $X\times_YT$, so $v:V\to X$ is pointed etale and $H$-equivariant [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change, lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. The projection of a finite module onto a direct factor is finite (project a generating family), so $p$ is finite. Its square with $q$ commutes by construction.

source.place: Tag 0BST (lemma-inertia-invariants-etale), final paragraph: selected component and its invariant base

proof.text: The affine scheme $X_a$ is normal Noetherian, hence a finite disjoint union of normal integral components by [rem-pc-regular-normal]. The scheme $X_a\times_{Y_a}T$ is Noetherian: its ring $S$ is finite over the Noetherian $B$, and a finite module algebra is of finite type, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] applies. On each of the preceding components its projection is etale; [lem-fin-etale-normal-components] therefore makes it a finite union of normal integral open-and-closed schemes. Thus $V$ is normal Noetherian, with finitely many integral clopen components. Let $W$ be the component containing its unique point over $\mathfrak p$. Every $h\in H$ fixes this point, hence preserves $W$. The idempotent of $W$ is consequently in $S_1^H=B$ and is nonzero. Since $B$ is a domain it is $1$. Hence $V=W$ is integral. The map $v$ has nonempty open image by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-morphism-open-map]; that image meets the given dense free open of $X$. An element acting identically on $V$ fixes a geometric point in this intersection and is therefore $1$. This proves faithfulness on $V$.

source.place: Tag 033M (normal Noetherian components); more-algebra.tex/algebra.tex Tag 033C for etale normal ascent; morphisms.tex Tag 03WT (etale maps are open)

proof.text: For surjectivity, $B=S_1^H\hookrightarrow S_1$ is injective and integral by [lem-dl-a1-finite-invariant-prime-orbits-residues], so [lem-weil-pbc-integral-injective-lying-over] makes $p$ surjective. For every principal open $D(c)\subset T$, the localization $B_c$ is etale and flat over $B$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-finite-presentation-localization, lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-flat]. Flat invariants give $(S_1\otimes_B B_c)^H=B_c$ [lem-dl-a1-flat-base-change-finite-invariants]. These principal opens form a basis, so $\mathcal O_T=(p_*\mathcal O_V)^H$. Fix any algebraically closed geometric point of $T$ and two geometric lifts in $V$. Their projections to $X$ lie in one $G$-orbit by the hypothesis on $q$; the element carrying one to the other also carries the lifted points in $X\times_YT$, since it fixes the base coordinate. It must preserve the factor $V$, because the factors are disjoint. Its stabilizer is exactly $H$ by Step 4. Thus the geometric fibres of $p$ are precisely the $H$-orbits.

source.place: Tag 0BST selected-component quotient; algebra.tex Tag 00GQ (lying over); more-algebra.tex Tag 0BRH (flat invariants)

proof.text: Let $U\subseteq Y$ be any dense open over which $q$ is etale. The nonempty integral $T$ maps etale to $Y$ and hence openly by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-morphism-open-map], so $T_U=T\times_YU$ is nonempty. It is an open subscheme of integral $T$, hence integral and connected. Surjectivity gives $V_U\ne\varnothing$; it too is open in integral $V$, hence connected. The pullback of $q|_U$ to $T_U$ is finite etale [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence, lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]. Its clopen restriction $p_U:V_U\to T_U$ is finite etale by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-clopen-restriction-rank]. Its rank is constant on connected $T_U$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-flat-rank-iso]. Finite etale local splitting [lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-etale-local-split] identifies this rank with the number of geometric points in each fibre. The inverse image in $V_U$ of the dense free open of $X$ is a nonempty open: $v$ is open and its restriction to the nonempty open $V_U$ is open. Choose a geometric point there. Its $H$-stabilizer is trivial, and Step 6 identifies its entire fibre with its $H$-orbit, so that fibre has $|H|$ elements. Every fibre therefore has $|H|$ elements and is a transitive $H$-set; the orbit-stabilizer formula makes every stabilizer trivial. Thus $p_U$ is the asserted connected finite etale $H$-torsor, in the explicit fibrewise sense in the statement.

source.place: Tag 04MH (finite locally free rank), and etale.tex Tag 04HN (finite etale local splitting); generic freeness plus constant rank

proof.text: If $n=|H|$ is invertible in $\kappa(x)$, it is nonzero in that field and therefore nonzero in the subfield $\kappa(y)$. Thus $n\notin\mathfrak p$ in $B$. Replace $T$ by $D(n)$ and $V$ by its inverse image. This is a pointed affine etale refinement, $n$ is invertible on it, and both schemes remain nonempty normal integral Noetherian (their rings are localizations). The finite quotient, invariant-sheaf, orbit and torsor conclusions restrict to this open by their formulas in Steps 4--7; in particular the actions remain faithful by the same dense-free-point argument. If the invertibility condition is absent, make no such replacement.

source.place: Tag 0BST, permissible principal localization; elementary unit-locus restriction

proof.text:
Put $R=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{Y,\bar y}$ and $C=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{X,\bar x}$. The pointed etale maps $T\to Y$ and $V\to X$ identify their strict local rings with $R$ and $C$, respectively, by [lem-trf-ind-etale-strict-local-invariance]. The chosen geometric fibre of $p$ has a single point: Step 3 gave a single prime with purely inseparable residue extension. Apply [lem-trf-finite-base-strict-localization] to $p$ at the pointing of $T$. There is only one summand, giving the canonical identification $\operatorname{Spec}C=V\times_T\operatorname{Spec}R$, with $C$ finite local over $R$. It is $H$-equivariant, since $H$ fixes the selected geometric point and the decomposition maps are the structural pointed maps. The structural map $B\to R$ is flat by [lem-sbc-affine-strict-henselization-structural-flat]. With $S_1^H=B$, flat invariants [lem-dl-a1-flat-base-change-finite-invariants] give
$$C^H=(R\otimes_B S_1)^H=R\otimes_B S_1^H=R.$$
These are the canonical structural maps, rather than an abstract isomorphism of rings.

source.place: Tags 05WR and 0GIP (finite strict localization and etale invariance); more-algebra.tex Tag 0BRH (flat invariants); ILO VI p.74 after 3.5

proof.text: Finally write $E=\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)=S_1$, a normal domain by Step 5. The strict local ring $C$ is its filtered pointed-etale colimit and is local [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit, lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-colimit-normal-local-domain]: $C$ is a normal domain and $E\to C$ is injective. If $h\in H$ acts identically on $C$, equivariance of this injection gives $h(e)=e$ for every $e\in E$. Thus $h$ acts identically on $V$ and is $1$ by Step 5. This proves strict-local faithfulness as well as normality. All constructions were pointed refinements of $T_0$; the regularity used was that of $Y$, and neither tameness nor excellence entered the construction.

source.place: Tag 06DI (lemma-henselization-normal), together with the injective-colimit formulation and pointed functoriality

Live, the item is still unsplit and has no repair note. The statement is kept in full; the only stmt_deps change adds pointed-etale-neighbourhoods, which the statement uses. Steps 1-4 follow 0BST in order: flat invariants, the geometric-point idempotent split, one prime per factor with purely inseparable residue field, the equivariant refinement after principal localization, and the transitive-product inertia factor. I checked I=Stab_G(x̄) through the Ω-point t∘g=t. Step 5: integrality via the H-invariant component idempotent lying in S_1^H=B (a domain, so the idempotent is 1); faithfulness via the open image of v meeting the dense free locus.
